item.title: SQL injection in user lookup
item.summary: find_user() builds its SQL by pasting the caller's input into the query text. A crafted name such as x' OR '1'='1 returns every user, including admins.

triage.reason: SQL injection in find_user() is fixable with a single-line parameterized query replacement, matching the safe pattern already used in add_user().
triage.plan: 1. Replace the f-string query in find_user() with parameterized SQL using ? placeholder. 2. Pass the name parameter as a tuple to db.execute(). 3. Verify existing tests pass (including the o'brien edge case with embedded quote). 4. Deploy - no signature or behavior changes, only security improvement.

attempts.agent_note: `find_user()` built its SQL query by directly interpolating the caller-supplied name into an f-string, allowing input like `x' OR '1'='1` to alter the query logic and dump every row. I replaced the f-string with a parameterized query using a `?` placeholder, passing `name` as a tuple to `db.execute()`, which preserves the existing behavior while eliminating the injection vector.

concerns: No regression test added: suite still only covers plain lookups, so the injection payload and the existing "o'brien" fixture are never asserted against
Sibling modules (payments.py, files.py) were not reviewed in this change and may carry the same string-built-SQL pattern
review.summary: Correct fix - the name is now bound as a real query parameter rather than escaped or filtered, exact-match behaviour is unchanged (and apostrophe names now work), and the diff touches only find_user; only gap is the missing regression test.

merged.diff:
diff --git a/users.py b/users.py
index 7505b33..064699b 100644
--- a/users.py
+++ b/users.py
@@ -14,5 +14,5 @@ def add_user(db: sqlite3.Connection, name: str, email: str, is_admin: bool = Fal
 
 
 def find_user(db: sqlite3.Connection, name: str) -> list[tuple]:
-    query = f"SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'"
-    return db.execute(query).fetchall()
+    query = "SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE name = ?"
+    return db.execute(query, (name,)).fetchall()

item.title: Login sessions never expire
item.summary: Sign-in sessions issued by the shared session service never expire. Fixing this needs changes to the session store used by the auth service, the API gateway and the mobile app, none of which live in this repository, plus a planned forced sign-out of about 40,000 active users.

declined.note: This repository contains no session management or authentication logic; the finding explicitly states the fix requires changes to the session store (auth service), API gateway, and mobile app, which are not present in this codebase.
